{{2026 Pakistan Super League Teams|main=y}}

The '''2026 Pakistan Super League''' (branded as '''HBL PSL 11''') was the eleventh edition of the [[Pakistan Super League]], a professional [[Twenty20]] [[cricket]] league organised by the [[Pakistan Cricket Board]] (PCB). This season marked the league's expansion from six to eight franchises, with [[Hyderabad Kingsmen]] and [[Rawalpindiz]] joining as new teams. It was played from 26 March to 3 May 2026, with 44 matches held in [[Karachi]] and [[Lahore]].

[[Peshawar Zalmi]] won the tournament, defeating debutant [[Hyderabad Kingsmen]] by five wickets in the [[2026 Pakistan Super League final|final]] to win their second PSL title.<ref>{{cite web |access-date=4 May 2026 |title=Hardie owns big stage to help Zalmi lift second PSL title |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/pakistan-super-league-2026-1515734/hyderabad-kingsmen-vs-peshawar-zalmi-final-1527595/match-report |website=[[Cricinfo|ESPNcricinfo]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Ali |first=Akber |date=3 May 2026 |title=Peshawar Zalmi beat Hyderabad Kingsmen by 5 wickets, lift PSL trophy a second time |url=https://www.dawn.com/news/1997223 |access-date=4 May 2026 |work=[[Dawn (newspaper)|Dawn]]}}</ref>

==Background ==
After the conclusion of the tenth season in 2025, the initial ten-year franchise agreements for the six original teams expired. The Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) engaged [[Ernst & Young]] to conduct a valuation of the league's assets to set new terms for the next decade (2026–2035).<ref>{{cite news |title=PSL initiates asset valuation process |author=Saleem Khaliq |url=https://tribune.com.pk/story/2563543/p |work=The Express Tribune |date=27 August 2025 |accessdate=5 March 2026}}</ref> In October 2025, [[HBL Pakistan]] renewed its title sponsorship for PSL for the next two years.<ref>{{cite news |title=Franchise owners will have right to match new team valuation or walk away, says PSL CEO Salman Naseer |url=https://www.dawn.com/news/1951973 |work=Dawn |date=29 October 2025 |accessdate=23 March 2026}}</ref>

In November 2025, five of the then-existing six franchises successfully renewed their contracts under the new financial model except [[Multan Sultans]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Ali Tareen opts not to extend Multan Sultans' PSL contract |url=https://www.geo.tv/latest/635536 |access-date=6 March 2026 |publisher=Geo News |date=25 November 2025}}</ref> As part of the PCB's plan to expand the league from six to eight teams, an auction for two new franchises was held on 8 January 2026. Six cities were shortlisted for consideration: [[Faisalabad]], [[Gilgit]], [[Hyderabad, Sindh|Hyderabad]], [[Muzaffarabad]], [[Rawalpindi]] and [[Sialkot]]. Following the auction, [[Hyderabad Kingsmen]] and Sialkot were selected as the seventh and eighth teams, with ownership rights acquired by FKS Group and OZ Developers respectively.<ref>{{Cite news |author=Zulfiqar Baig |date=8 January 2026 |title=Sialkot, Hyderabad enter HBL PSL after Rs3.6b auction |url=https://tribune.com.pk/story/2585422/p |access-date=8 January 2026 |work=The Express Tribune}}</ref>

[[Ali Tareen]], previous owner of Multan Sultans franchise, announced that he would not renew his agreement with the PCB, and cited financial losses and disagreements regarding the league's management.<ref>{{cite news |title=Ali Tareen bows out as Multan Sultans owner after franchise denied renewal |url=https://www.dawn.com/news/1957302 |work=[[Dawn (newspaper)|Dawn]] |date=25 November 2025 |access-date=26 November 2025}}</ref> Thus, PCB decided to resell the franchise through an auction on 9 February 2026,<ref>{{cite news |author=Mohammad Yaqoob |date=10 February 2026 |title=Multan Sultans sold for record price but owners opt for Rawalpindi rebrand |url=https://www.dawn.com/news/1972137 |work=Dawn |access-date=5 March 2026}}</ref> where Walee Technologies acquired it and rebranded the identity to [[Rawalpindiz]] after relocating. Later, Sialkot owners sold the franchise to CD Ventures, who rebranded and brought back the Multan Sultans.<ref>{{cite news |author=Mohammad Yaqoob |title=Multan Sultans return to PSL at Sialkot's expense |url=https://www.dawn.com/news/1978171 |work=Dawn |date=4 March 2026 |accessdate=5 March 2026 |archive-date=7 March 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260307145430/https://www.dawn.com/news/1978171 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://jang.com.pk/news/1565670 |title={{Nq|ٹیم 'پنڈیز' نے سوشل میڈیا اکاؤنٹس پر نام 'راولپنڈیز' کردیا}} |date=17 March 2026 |accessdate=18 March 2026 |work=Daily Jang |author={{Nq|فیضان لاکھانی}}}}</ref>

===Trophy===
The trophy for the season was named "Infinity". Designed by Hanif Jewellers, it was handcrafted by 18 artisans. It featured a circular base with eight [[emerald]]-cut jewels representing eight teams. It had two golden curved arms rising to hold a crescent and a star along with hundreds of small crystals. It was revealed on 11 March at National Bank Stadium, Karachi, and toured across the country.<ref>{{cite news |title=PCB unveils 'Infinity Trophy' ahead of HBL PSL XI |url=https://tribune.com.pk/story/2597062/i |work=The Express Tribune |date=11 March 2026 |accessdate=23 March 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=PSL 11 trophy unveiled as league enters new era |url=https://www.dawn.com/news/1981120 |work=Dawn |date=12 March 2026 |access-date=23 March 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |author=Muhammad Saleem |title=HBL-PSL 'Infinity' Trophy tour reaches Lahore |url=https://www.brecorder.com/news/40412614 |work=Business Recorder |date=23 March 2026 |accessdate=23 March 2026}}</ref>

===Prize money===
The champions received {{US$|500,000}}, while the runner-up team received {{US$|300,000}}. Moreover, a {{US$|200,000}} reward was awarded to the "best franchise contributing towards cricket development".<ref>{{cite news |title=Mohsin Naqvi announces revised prize money for next PSL edition |url=https://www.geo.tv/latest/634720 |publisher=Geo News |date=21 November 2025 |accessdate=5 March 2025 |author=Sohail Imran}}</ref>

==Teams and squads==
{{Main|2026 Pakistan Super League personnel signings and auction}}

The player auction for the eleventh season was held on 11 February 2026 in [[Lahore]], Pakistan. It was the first time in PSL history that players were selected through an [[Player auction|auction system]], replacing the [[Draft (sports)|draft method]] that had been used since the league began in [[2016 Pakistan Super League players draft|2016]]. Team purse was capped at {{PKR|45 crore}} and was allowed to be extended to {{PKR|50.5 crore}} to allow direct signing of one foreign player who had not featured in a previous season. Franchises were allowed to retain up to four players, one in each category before the auction; new franchises were allowed to sign four players to match the retentions of the other six franchises.<ref>{{Cite web |date=25 November 2025 |title=PCB announces HBL PSL XI players auction on Feb 11 |url=https://tribune.com.pk/story/2588987/p |work=The Express Tribune |access-date=28 January 2026}}</ref> 888 players, including local and foreign, registered for the auction at 4 different base prices.<ref>{{cite news |title=PSL 2026 Auction: Full List Of Players With Base Price For Pakistan Super League Auction |url=https://www.wisden.com/series/psl-2026/cricket-news/psl-2026-auction-full-list-of-players-with-base-price-for-pakistan-super-league-auction |work=[[Wisden]] |date=10 February 2026 |accessdate=5 March 2026}}</ref>

Rawalpindiz signed Pakistani pacer [[Naseem Shah]] for {{PKR|8.65 crore}}, making him the most expensive player in the auction. Additionally, they secured New Zealand all-rounder [[Daryl Mitchell (New Zealand cricketer)|Daryl Mitchell]] for {{PKR|8 crore}}, the most expensive overseas signing.<ref>{{Cite news |author=Asher Butt |url=https://www.thenews.pk/print/1398690 |title=Steve Smith tops PSL 11 auction as Sialkot Stallionz secure record signing |work=[[thenews.com.pk|The News]] |date=12 February 2026 |access-date=5 March 2026}}</ref> Player transfer window was opened from 12 March to 18 March, allowing franchises to trade players. Multan Sultans' salary cap was increased by {{PKR|1.2 crore}} to allow two additional signings, making the full squad of 22 players.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Alam |first1=Sher |title=Multan Sultans Given Special Salary Cap Ahead of PSL 11 Transfer Window |url=https://propakistani.pk/2026/03/12/multan-sultans-given-special-salary-cap-ahead-of-psl-11-transfer-window/ |website=ProPakistani |date=12 March 2026}}</ref>

On 26 March, the PCB introduced a new rule that each captain could submit two sets of [[first XI]] to the referee before beginning the match.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://jang.com.pk/news/1568132 |title={{Nq|پی ایس ایل 11 میں نیا قانون متعارف کرادیا گیا}} |author={{Nq|سہیل عمران}} |date=26 March 2026 |accessdate=30 March 2026 |work=Daily Jang}}</ref>

The PCB revealed the venue details on 10 March 2026. Lahore hosted the opening match as well as the final.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.geonewsurdu.tv/latest/429611- |title={{Nq|پاکستان سپر لیگ 11 کے شیڈول کا اعلان کردیا گیا}} |date=10 March 2026 |access-date=11 March 2026 |author={{Nq|سہیل عمران}} |work=[[Geo News]] |language=ur}}</ref>

Initially the tournament was scheduled to be held across six cities, but due to the [[economic impact of the 2026 Iran war]], the [[Government of Pakistan]] (GoP) and [[Pakistan Cricket Board]] (PCB) announced on 22 March that the tournament would be played in only two cities, Lahore and Karachi, temporarily [[Behind closed doors (sport)|behind closed doors]] to reduce movement to save fuel. The opening ceremony was also cancelled.<ref>{{cite news |author=Ammara Khan |title=PSL to commence without spectators, matches limited to Karachi, Lahore |url=https://tribune.com.pk/story/2598704/p |work=[[The Express Tribune]] |date=22 March 2026 |access-date=23 March 2026}}</ref><ref name=revsc>{{cite news |author=Jai Rai |title=Pakistan Super League to be held without spectators |url=https://gulfnews.com/1.500482645 |work=[[Gulf News]] |date=22 March 2026 |access-date=23 March 2026}}</ref> Later, on the request of franchise owners, Prime Minister [[Shehbaz Sharif]] allowed the fans to attend the [[#Playoffs|playoffs]] and the [[2026 Pakistan Super League final|final]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Cricket fans allowed to attend playoff matches in Pakistan Super League |url=https://www.gulftoday.ae/sport/2026/04/27/cricket-fans-allowed-to-attend-playoff-matches-in-pakistan-super-league |work=[[Gulf Today]] |access-date=29 April 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |date=28 April 2026 |title=Spectators allowed to witness all PSL playoffs |url=https://www.dawn.com/news/1995630 |work=[[Dawn (newspaper)|Dawn]] |access-date=29 April 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Mohammed |first1=Shamseer |date=25 April 2026 |title=Good news for fans: PSL 11 final to be played with full crowd |url=https://gulfnews.com/sport/cricket/good-news-for-fans-psl-11-final-to-be-played-with-full-crowd-1.500518951 |work=[[Gulf News]] |access-date=27 April 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |author=Danyal Rasool |date=25 April 2026 |title=PSL 2026 final to be played in front of fans in Lahore |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/psl-2026-final-to-be-played-in-front-of-fans-in-lahore-1533568 |work=[[Cricinfo|ESPNcricinfo]] |access-date=28 April 2026}}</ref>

==Match officials==
On 23 March 2026, the PCB announced the list of fifteen [[Umpire (cricket)|umpires]] and eight [[match referee]]s for the league stage.<ref>{{cite news |title=پی ایس ایل 11 کے میچ آفیشلز کا اعلان |url=https://jang.com.pk/news/1567070 |work=jang.com.pk |language=ur}}</ref> They included four members of the [[Elite Panel of ICC Umpires]] and nine of the PCB domestic umpires. [[Roshan Mahanama]] returned to extend his record of 71 matches as a match referee in the PSL. [[Richie Richardson]], [[Allahudien Paleker]], and [[Sharfuddoula]] made their first appearances as match officials in PSL. [[Alex Wharf]] and [[Ahsan Raza]] were named as on-field umpires for the opening match with [[Asif Yaqoob]] as television umpire and Tariq Rasheed as fourth umpire.<ref>{{cite news |title=Richardson set for PSL debut as PCB unveils match officials for season 11 |url=https://www.nation.com.pk/24-Mar-2026/richardson-set-psl-debut-pcb-unveils-match-officials-season-11 |work=The Nation |date=24 March 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Richie Richardson to make debut as PSL 11 match officials confirmed |url=https://www.geosuper.tv/latest/54503-richie-richardson-to-make-debut-as-psl-11-match-officials-confirmed |website=www.geosuper.tv}}</ref>

==Marketing==
{{Further|Khelenge Beat Pe}}
The season's logo variant was revealed on 4 March,<ref>{{cite news |url=https://a-sports.tv/psl-11-logo-unveiled-ahead-historic-eight-team-season |title=WATCH: PSL 11 logo unveiled ahead historic eight-team season |date=4 March 2026 |accessdate=25 March 2026 |publisher=A Sports}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.geosuper.tv/latest/53978 |title=WATCH: PSL 11 official logo released |date=4 March 2026 |accessdate=25 March 2026 |publisher=Geo Super}}</ref> with an official nomenclature, HBL PSL 11,{{efn|name=nc|1=[https://www.pcb.com.pk/press-release-detail/pcb-announces-revised-schedule-for-hbl-psl-11.html Official nomenclature]}} and the official anthem was released on 24 March, titled "Khelenge Beat Pe".<ref>{{cite news |url=https://a-sports.tv/psl-11-official-anthem-khelenge-beat-pe-released |title=PSL 11 official anthem 'Khelenge Beat Pe' released |date=24 March 2026 |accessdate=25 March 2026 |publisher=A Sports |author=Huzaifa Gaba}}</ref>

===Broadcast===
In February 2026, PCB held three bids for [[broadcasting rights]]; however, the rights for India were withheld. Walee Technologies, who were also the owners of the Rawalpindiz franchise, won all bids, including the international rights, with a 149 percent increase in value as compared to the previous rights cycle, although the official financial figures were not disclosed. Also, the local broadcasting and streaming rights were sold for {{PKR|2611 [[crore]]}} for a four-year period.<ref>{{cite news |title=PCB withholds PSL 11 broadcast rights in India |url=https://www.geo.tv/latest/648835 |publisher=Geo News |date=3 February 2026 |accessdate=5 March 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |date=4 February 2026 |title=Sale of media rights for PSL 11 fetches massive increase |url=https://www.dawn.com/news/1970889 |access-date=23 March 2026 |work=Dawn}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |author=Saleem Khaliq |date=28 February 2026 |title=PCB secures biggest media rights deal for HBL PSL |url=https://tribune.com.pk/story/2595043/p |access-date=5 March 2026 |work=The Express Tribune}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |date=1 March 2026 |title=PSL broadcast rights sold for Rs26.11 bn |url=https://www.dawn.com/news/1976772 |access-date=23 March 2026 |work=Dawn}}</ref>

The names for the commentary panel and presenters were revealed on 23 March. Notably, [[Shoaib Malik]] made his debut in Urdu commentary after retiring from the game, as he had played in the previous ten seasons.<ref>{{cite news |date=23 March 2026 |title=Commentary panel announced for PSL 11 |url=https://www.24newshd.tv/23-Mar-2026/commentary-panel-announced-psl-11 |access-date=23 March 2026 |publisher=24 Digital |author=Rana Azhar}}</ref> Due to no on-field spectators, this edition was a watch-from-home event, having a dedicated Urdu feed along with a match analysis talk show which was introduced for the first time.<ref>{{cite news |date=26 March 2026 |title=PSL 11 broadcast overhaul promises immersive cricket experience for fans |url=https://www.pakistantoday.com.pk/2026/03/26/psl-11-broadcast-overhaul-promises-immersive-cricket-experience-for-fans |access-date=27 March 2026 |work=Pakistan Today}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |date=22 March 2026 |title=Fuel crisis forces PCB to announce revised PSL 2026 schedule, Lahore & Karachi only venues |url=https://www.insidesport.in/cricket/fuel-crisis-forces-pcb-to-announce-revised-psl-2026-schedule-lahore-karachi-only-venues |access-date=27 March 2026 |work=Inside Sport |author=Krishnendu Banerjee}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |date=23 March 2026 |title=Stay Home And Watch PSL 2026 Matches On Television: Mohsin Naqvi Orders Cricket Fans To Save Fuel Amid Iran War |url=https://www.thedailyjagran.com/cricket/pakistan-super-league-2026-to-be-played-behind-closed-doors-amid-west-asia-conflict-10304639 |access-date=27 March 2026 |work=The Daily Jagran |author=Gurmeet Batra}}</ref>

==League stage==
===Format===
Due to the expansion to eight teams, this edition was played under a revised format with a total of 44 matches, replacing the [[double round-robin]] format used in previous editions. The teams were divided into two virtual groups of four; each team played twice against the other teams in its group and once against each team in the opposite group, resulting in a total of ten league-stage matches per team. The top four teams in the overall standings qualified for the [[#Playoffs|playoffs]], which were played under the [[page playoff system]] to determine the champion.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://jang.com.pk/en/54993-psl-2026-schedule-how-many-matches-will-be-played-in-11th-edition-news |title=PSL 2026 schedule: How many matches will be played in 11th edition? |date=16 December 2025 |accessdate=5 March 2026 |author=Bushra Saleem |work=[[Daily Jang]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Alam |first1=Sher |title=All You Need to Know About PSL 11 Format |url=https://propakistani.pk/2026/03/11/all-you-need-to-know-about-psl-11-format/ |website=ProPakistani |access-date=29 March 2026 |date=11 March 2026}}</ref>

* [[Karachi Kings]] scored their lowest total in Pakistan Super League.
* [[Peshawar Zalmi]] recorded the largest win by runs in Pakistan Super League.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.thedailystar.net/sports/cricket/news/rana-rips-through-karachi-peshawar-seal-record-win-4148126 |title=Rana rips through Karachi as Peshawar seal record win |work=[[The Daily Star (Bangladesh)|The Daily Star]] |date=10 April 2026 |access-date=16 April 2026}}</ref>

==Controversies==

===Naseem Shah tweet===
[[Maryam Nawaz]], the [[Chief Minister of Punjab (Pakistan)|Chief Minister of Punjab]] and niece of Prime Minister [[Shehbaz Sharif]], attended the opening match along with several political figures,<ref>{{cite news |title=Maryam Nawaz attends simple opening ceremony of HBL PSL 11 |url=https://www.nation.com.pk/26-Mar-2026/maryam-nawaz-attends-simple-opening-ceremony-hbl-psl-11 |work=The Nation |author=Azhar Khan |date=26 March 2026 |accessdate=30 March 2026}}</ref> despite the [[Pakistan Cricket Board|PCB]] having restricted the general public at the stadiums.<ref name=revsc/> A controversy emerged with a tweet from the official [[X (social network)|X]] account of [[Rawalpindiz]]'s fast bowler [[Naseem Shah]], criticizing Nawaz's reception. Although the tweet was later deleted and Shah issued a clarification claiming his account had been compromised, the PCB issued him a show-cause notice, asserting that the incident breached the terms of his central contract and the board's media regulations regarding public criticism of officials.<ref>{{cite news |title={{Nq|سینٹرل کنٹریکٹ کی خلاف ورزی پر نسیم شاہ کو شوکاز نوٹس جاری}} |url=https://jang.com.pk/news/1568475 |work=Daily Jang |author={{Nq|سہیل عمران}} |date=27 March 2026 |accessdate=30 March 2026}}</ref> Shah was fined {{PKR|2 [[crore]]}} and his social media manager was blacklisted from managing any player under a PCB contract.<ref>{{cite news |author=Suramya Kaushik |title=PCB fines Naseem Shah over social media post |url=https://www.reuters.com/sports/cricket/pcb-fines-naseem-shah-over-social-media-post-2026-03-30/ |access-date=2 April 2026 |work=Reuters |date=30 March 2026}}</ref>

===Security protocol breach===
[[Punjab Police (Pakistan)|Punjab Police]] wrote a formal letter to the PSL CEO, stating that on 28 March, [[Lahore Qalandars]]' captain [[Shaheen Shah Afridi]] and teammate [[Sikandar Raza]] breached a security protocol at the team hotel by bringing four visitors to a hotel room, despite the permission request by Qalandars team owner Sameen Rana being denied by PSL officials. Police requested a review of the incident and demanded necessary action to prevent future violations.<ref>{{cite news |title=In letter to PSL CEO, police detail alleged security protocol breach |url=https://www.dawn.com/news/1986590 |work=Dawn |author=Asif Chaudhry |date=30 March 2026 |accessdate=30 March 2026}}</ref> Raza later stated he was unaware of the updated protocols, noting that meeting family members at the hotel had been allowed in previous seasons.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://urdu.arynews.tv/sikandar-raza-truth-last-over-umpires-will-tell |title={{Nq|آخری اوور کی حقیقت امپائرز بتائیں گے، میں نے کچھ نہیں کیا، سکندر رضا}} |date=29 March 2026 |accessdate=30 March 2026 |publisher=ARY News}}</ref> Lahore Qalandars fined Afridi {{PKR|10 lakh}} after an inquiry, and the PCB issued new, stricter regulations regarding team accommodation.<ref>{{cite news |title=PCB tightens hotel security after Afridi incident |url=https://tribune.com.pk/story/2600481/p |work=The Express Tribune |date=1 April 2026 |accessdate=2 April 2026 |author=Saleem Khaliq}}</ref>

===Ball tampering controversy===
On 29 March, on-field umpires found that [[Lahore Qalandars]] had violated [[Laws of Cricket#Unfair play|Law 41.3.2]], which deals with [[ball tampering]]. As a result, they were penalized five runs, which were awarded to [[Karachi Kings]] during the match. The match referee conducted an investigation immediately after the match, where Lahore Qalandars player [[Fakhar Zaman (cricketer)|Fakhar Zaman]] denied the allegations of tampering.<ref name=tamp>{{cite news |title=Lahore punished for ball tampering in PSL defeat |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/cricket/articles/cx2475glyjwo |publisher=[[BBC Sport]] |author=Matthew Henry |date=30 March 2026 |accessdate=30 March 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title={{Nq|گیند سے چھیڑ چھاڑ: لاہور قلندرز کے فخر زمان کو لیول تھری جرم پر چارج کردیا گیا}} |url=https://jang.com.pk/news/1569053 |work=[[Daily Jang]] |author={{Nq|سہیل عمران}} |date=30 March 2026 |accessdate=30 March 2026}}</ref> A second investigation held on 31 March 2026 resulted in Zaman receiving a two-match ban.<ref>{{cite news |author=Timothy Abraham |title=Fakhar gets two-match ban for ball tampering in PSL |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/cricket/articles/cy81n47yxndo |publisher=[[BBC Sport]] |date=31 March 2026 |accessdate=2 April 2026}}</ref>

===Inappropriate gesture===
On 29 March, the PCB fined [[Hasan Ali (cricketer)|Hasan Ali]] of Karachi Kings 10% of his match fee for violating [[Laws of Cricket#Setting up the game|Law 2.5]], which deals with inappropriate language or gestures against a dismissed batsman. He was found to have made such a gesture toward [[Haseebullah Khan]] of Lahore Qalandars.<ref>{{cite news |title={{Nq|کوڈ آف کنڈکٹ کی خلاف ورزی: کراچی کنگز کے حسن علی پر جرمانہ عائد}} |url=https://jang.com.pk/news/1569075 |work=Daily Jang |author={{Nq|سہیل عمران}} |date=30 March 2026 |accessdate=30 March 2026}}</ref>
